blocks.goal: Extract the protocol-management responsibility (allowed URL protocols per tag+attribute) from Safelist into a dedicated SafelistProtocols class to reduce the number of public methods on Safelist and reduce its overall method count and LOC.

expected_impact.rationale: The public protocol-related APIs addProtocols(...) and removeProtocols(...) are moved out of Safelist into SafelistProtocols, reducing Safelist's public method count by 2. Supporting private helpers and the protocols map are also moved, reducing total methods and LOC in Safelist and isolating the protocol logic into a cohesive class.

ops.details: Create new class org.jsoup.safety.SafelistProtocols that encapsulates the protocols map (Map<TagName, Map<AttributeKey, Set<Protocol>>>) and provides the protocol-related APIs: addProtocols(String tag, String attribute, String... protocols), removeProtocols(String tag, String attribute, String... removeProtocols), getProtocols(Safelist.TagName tag, Safelist.AttributeKey key) (returns Set<Safelist.Protocol> or null), hasProtocol(Safelist.TagName tag, Safelist.AttributeKey key) (boolean), and an internal isSafeProtocol(String value, Set<Safelist.Protocol>) plus internal getProtocolValue(Element el, Attribute attr) helpers. Also add a copy constructor SafelistProtocols(SafelistProtocols copy) for deep copy. The new class is placed in the same package (org.jsoup.safety) and uses the nested types from Safelist (TagName, AttributeKey, Protocol) to avoid duplicating typed-value classes.

Move the field 'private final Map<TagName, Map<AttributeKey, Set<Protocol>>> protocols' out of Safelist into SafelistProtocols as a private final field. In Safelist, replace the removed map with a new final field 'private final SafelistProtocols protocolsManager;' and initialize it in constructors (default and copy) so behavior is preserved. The Safelist copy constructor will delegate deep-copy of protocols to the SafelistProtocols copy constructor.

Move the protocol-related methods from Safelist into SafelistProtocols: public Safelist addProtocols(String tag, String attribute, String... protocols) and public Safelist removeProtocols(String tag, String attribute, String... removeProtocols) (converted into SafelistProtocols methods that return SafelistProtocols for chaining). Also move private helpers that are directly tied to protocol handling: private String getProtocolValue(Element el, Attribute attr) and private boolean isSafeProtocol(String value, Set<Protocol> protocols). Remove these methods from Safelist. The moved methods in SafelistProtocols will use Safelist.TagName, Safelist.AttributeKey, and Safelist.Protocol nested types.

Update internal Safelist usages that referenced the moved 'protocols' map or used the moved helpers. Specifically: in isSafeAttribute(...) replace direct access to the protocols map with calls to protocolsManager.getProtocols(tag, key) and use the returned Set<Protocol> when invoking protocol checks; in shouldAbsUrl(TagName, AttributeKey) replace 'protocols.get(tag) ... containsKey(key)' checks with protocolsManager.hasProtocol(tag, key); update the Safelist constructors and copy constructor to initialize protocolsManager and copy protocol state via protocolsManager (using its copy constructor). No external production call sites are wrapped; callers that previously invoked Safelist.addProtocols/removeProtocols will be updated by the deterministic post-processing step (UPDATE_TESTS) when needed.

Ensure SafelistProtocols.java has the necessary imports (org.jsoup.nodes.Element, org.jsoup.nodes.Attribute, java.util.*) and update Safelist.java imports if necessary when referencing the new SafelistProtocols type.

Update related tests affected by this refactoring block so the configured build command passes. Adjust imports, package references, moved class references, constructors, and assertions only when required. Do not change production behavior through tests.
